convoLines.text: They speak. You understand none of it. "Fuck you." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
They speak; the translation falters.
"Hm. Almost." Catalina corrects the one word, gently, like setting a bone. "Again." You say it right. They nod, satisfied with both of you.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"I stay where I'm useful. Right now that's here. Columbus, Ohio is a direction, not a plan. Here is a plan, even if it's a hard one."
"Still on whether you're staying."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Marta was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out. Seen worse."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Funny thing: Still on what they confided."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Aaliyah grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Aaliyah is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Marta is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I rinse the cup twice at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They speak. You understand none of it. "No, no." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They answer at length. They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
They answer at length. A smile, tired but real.
They answer at length. You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I be honest? We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Maeve doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Heh. Still on what's been happening."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"I'm picking up Ethan's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Aaliyah nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They speak. You understand none of it.
"This one — Birch Sap. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly. "Food?"
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.

They speak; the translation falters.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what they confided — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? '...Anyway. What did you want to ask?' Give it time."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Aaliyah has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided. That's still where we are."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.

"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind? I mean it."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Ethan died... I keep expecting to see Ethan at the fire. Stupid."
"I rinse the cup twice for Ethan, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Maeve nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."

"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about George?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my older brother, George. Was taken at the Scattering. He taught me to swim. The boring half. Sure. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Impress Us. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening. Extremely normal, all of it."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took you — Impress Us, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Aaliyah nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Ruth has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Catalina is gone and Grace is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"About grief — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"I keep turning over the last thing Grace said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet. This isn't new."
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that. Think, then act."
"We lost Catalina and Grace. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Catalina nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Permit me: Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.

lastSay: d61: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Ruth Goldstein is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d61: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d61: 🕯️ Ruth Goldstein is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d61: What Ruth kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d61: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
